findings.title: Emails are keyed off raw `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the unfiltered input. Emails already on the booking, which were dropped from `uniqueGuests`, are still in `guests`. Those existing attendees get the 'scheduled' email meant for brand-new guests instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead, and compare emails case-insensitively.

findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses `&&` instead of `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner = isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for admins and owners, and `isTeamOwner` is true only for owners. The `&&` therefore restricts access to owners and wrongly denies team admins. It also runs two redundant membership queries even when the caller is the organizer. The intent is clearly `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The existing-attendee check (`guest === attendee.email`) is also case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to `a@x.com`. The server also never dedupes within `guests`, so a direct API call with the same email twice creates duplicate attendee rows. Normalise emails (lowercase/trim) before every comparison and dedupe the input.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, and a failure leaves DB and calendar inconsistent
findings.body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, not the booking owner's credentials. The booking's calendar event lives in the organizer's calendar. When a team admin or an attendee adds guests, the calendar is silently not updated, or the update fails. The attendees are already persisted by `prisma.booking.update` before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, which is outside the try/catch. If it throws, the request returns an error to the user, no emails are sent, and the guests are still saved. Use the organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials` is already loaded but unused), and handle calendar failures without losing the notification step.

findings.title: No check on booking status or whether the booking is in the past
findings.body: The handler never checks `booking.status` or `endTime`. A caller can add guests to cancelled, rejected, pending or already-finished bookings, and each guest is sent a 'CONFIRMED' calendar invite (`method: REQUEST`, `status: CONFIRMED` in the new email templates). The UI also adds the action to `editBookingActions`, which is shown for past confirmed and past pending bookings and for seated events. Seated events track attendees via `seatsReferences`, which this flow ignores. The server should reject non-accepted or past bookings, and probably seated events.

findings.title: Unbounded guest list lets any attendee trigger arbitrary email sends
findings.body: `guests` has no `.max()`. The handler lets any attendee, not just the host, add guests. Each added address gets a calendar invite and email sent from the organizer's name, and every existing attendee, the host and team members are also emailed. One request with hundreds of addresses is an easy spam/abuse vector and a load problem. Add a reasonable cap and consider restricting who may add guests.

findings.title: CalendarEvent omits `team`, so team-member emails never fire
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` loops over `calendarEvent.team?.members`, but `evt` never sets `team` (nor `bookingId`, `iCalUID`, `responses`, `hideCalendarNotes`). For team or round-robin bookings the extra hosts are therefore never notified, and the team-member branch is dead code. Populate the missing fields as other booking handlers do.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails and compares emails case-sensitively
findings.body: Every other sender here takes `eventTypeMetadata` and honours `disableStandardEmails` for host/attendee emails. `sendAddGuestsEmails` always emails organizer, team members and all attendees, so event types that disabled standard emails still get notifications. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is also case-sensitive, so a differently-cased match sends the wrong template.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed and the error is not logged
findings.body: The catch block does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without the caught `err`, so the failure reason is lost and ops cannot diagnose it. The request still returns success. At minimum, log the error with the repo logger.

findings.title: Stale validation error is never cleared
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true on a failed validation but is never reset when the user edits the emails, when a valid submission is made, in the mutation `onSuccess`, or when the dialog is closed via the overlay or Escape. Only the Cancel button resets it. After one invalid attempt the 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner stays visible even after fixing the input, and it reappears the next time the dialog opens. Reset it on `handleAdd` success and on input change/close.

findings.title: Error toast shows raw code and untranslated message; fallback is unreachable
findings.body: The message is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always a non-empty string, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never applies. Users see text like 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'. For tRPC input-validation failures `err.message` is a JSON blob of zod issues. Show `t(err.message)` only for known keys, otherwise fall back to `unable_to_add_guests`.

findings.title: Hard-coded English tooltip text
findings.body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is not passed through `t()`, unlike the rest of the component, so it is not localised. Add a translation key.

findings.title: No tests for new permission-sensitive mutation
findings.body: The PR adds a mutation with authorization logic, a blacklist filter, DB writes, calendar updates and several email templates, but no unit, integration or e2e tests. The role check, blacklist, dedupe and email-recipient selection would all benefit from tests, and several of the bugs above would likely have been caught by them.
